pairs: Fili,
Son,
eleemosynam pauperis ne defraudes,
you should not cheat the poor out of alms,
et oculos tuos ne transvertas a paupere.
nor should you avert your eyes from a poor man.
Animam esurientem ne despexeris,
You should not despise the hungry soul,
et non exasperes pauperem in inopia sua.
and you should not aggravate a poor man in his need.
Cor inopis ne afflixeris,
You should not afflict the heart of the needy,
et non protrahas datum angustianti.
and you should not delay an offer to someone in anguish.
Rogationem contribulati ne abjicias,
You should not make requests of one who is greatly troubled,
et non avertas faciem tuam ab egeno.
and you should not avert your face from the indigent.
Ab inope ne avertas oculos tuos propter iram:
You should not avert your eyes from the needy out of anger.
et non relinquas quærentibus tibi retro maledicere.
And you should not abandon those who seek help from you, so that they speak curses behind your back.
Maledicentis enim tibi in amaritudine animæ,
For the pleadings of him who speaks curses of you,
exaudietur deprecatio illius:
in the bitterness of his soul, will be heeded.
exaudiet autem eum qui fecit illum.
For the One who made him will heed him.
Congregationi pauperum affabilem te facito:
Make yourself a friend to the congregation of the poor,
et presbytero humilia animam tuam,
and humble your soul before an elder,
et magnato humilia caput tuum.
and humble your head before the great.
Declina pauperi sine tristitia aurem tuam,
Turn your ear without sadness toward the poor,
et redde debitum tuum,
and repay your debt,
et responde illi pacifica in mansuetudine.
and respond to him peacefully in meekness.
Libera eum qui injuriam patitur de manu superbi,
Free him who suffers injury at the hand of the arrogant,
et non acide feras in anima tua.
and do not carry animosity in your soul.
In judicando esto pupillis misericors ut pater,
In judging, be merciful to the orphan, like a father,
et pro viro matri illorum:
and be merciful to their mother, like a husband.
et eris tu velut filius Altissimi obediens,
And then you shall be like an obedient son of the Most High,
et miserebitur tui magis quam mater.
and he will take pity on you more than a mother would.
Sapientia filiis suis vitam inspirat:
Wisdom breathes life into her sons,
et suscipit inquirentes se,
and she lifts up those who are seeking her,
et præibit in via justitiæ.
and she will precede them in the way of justice.
Et qui illam diligit, diligit vitam,
And he who loves her loves life.
et qui vigilaverint ad illam complectentur placorem ejus.
And those who watch for her shall embrace her delights.
Qui tenuerint illam,
Those who hold to her will inherit life.
vitam hæreditabunt:
And whatever place she enters,
et quo introibit benedicet Deus.
God will bless.
Qui serviunt ei obsequentes erunt sancto:
Those who serve her will yield to what is holy.
et eos qui diligunt illam, diligit Deus.
And God loves those who love wisdom.
Qui audit illam judicabit gentes:
He who listens to her shall judge the nations.
et qui intuetur illam permanebit confidens.
And he who gazes upon her will remain secure.
Si crediderit ei,
If he believes in her,
hæreditabit illam,
he will inherit her,
et erunt in confirmatione creaturæ illius:
and whatever arises from him will be confirmed.
quoniam in tentatione ambulat cum eo,
For she walks with him through temptation,
et in primis eligit eum.
and she chooses him from the beginning.
Timorem,
She will lead fear
et metum,
and dread
et probationem inducet super illum:
and trials over him,
et cruciabit illum in tribulatione doctrinæ suæ,
and she will crucify him with the tribulation of her doctrine,
donec tentet eum in cogitationibus suis,
until she has tested him in his thoughts
et credat animæ illius.
and she can trust in his soul.
Et firmabit illum,
And then she will strengthen him,
et iter adducet directum ad illum,
and lead him along a straight path,
et lætificabit illum:
and rejoice in him.
et denudabit absconsa sua illi,
And she will disclose her secrets to him,
et thesaurizabit super illum scientiam et intellectum justitiæ.
and she will store up treasure, of the knowledge and understanding of justice, in him.
Si autem oberraverit,
But if he has wandered astray,
derelinquet eum,
she will leave him behind,
et tradet eum in manus inimici sui.
and she will deliver him into the hands of his enemy.
Fili,
Son,
conserva tempus,
be continually observant,
et devita a malo.
and keep away from evil.
Pro anima tua ne confundaris dicere verum:
For the sake of your soul, you should not be ashamed to speak the truth.
est enim confusio adducens peccatum,
For there is a shame that brings sin,
et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam.
and there is a shame that brings glory and grace.
Ne accipias faciem adversus faciem tuam,
You should not accept a face contrary to your own face,
nec adversus animam tuam mendacium.
nor should you accept a lie contrary to your own soul.
Ne reverearis proximum tuum in casu suo,
You should not enjoy the fall of your neighbor.
nec retineas verbum in tempore salutis.
Neither should you withhold words at an opportunity for salvation.
Non abscondas sapientiam tuam in decore suo:
You should not conceal your wisdom in her beauty.
in lingua enim sapientia dignoscitur:
For wisdom is discerned within speech.
et sensus,
And understanding
et scientia,
and knowledge
et doctrina in verbo sensati,
and doctrine are discerned in the words of those who understand
et firmamentum in operibus justitiæ.
and by their steadfastness in the works of justice.
Non contradicas verbo veritatis ullo modo,
You should not contradict a word of truth in any way. Otherwise,
et de mendacio ineruditionis tuæ confundere.
by a falsehood born of ignorance, you will be confounded.
Non confundaris confiteri peccata tua,
You should not be ashamed to confess your sins,
et ne subjicias te omni homini pro peccato.
but do not subject yourself to any man because of sin.
Noli resistere contra faciem potentis,
Do not choose to stand against the face of the powerful,
nec coneris contra ictum fluvii.
for you should not strive against the current of the river.
Pro justitia agonizare pro anima tua,
Suffer for justice, on behalf of your soul,
et usque ad mortem certa pro justitia:
and struggle, even unto death, on behalf of justice,
et Deus expugnabit pro te inimicos tuos.
and God will fight against your enemies on your behalf.
Noli citatus esse in lingua tua,
Do not choose to be quick with your words,
et inutilis,
nor unproductive
et remissus in operibus tuis.
or neglectful in your works.
Noli esse sicut leo in domo tua,
Do not choose to be like a lion in your house,
evertens domesticos tuos,
distressing those of your household,
et opprimens subjectos tibi.
and oppressing those who are subject to you.
Non sit porrecta manus tua ad accipiendum,
Do not let your hand be open when receiving,
et ad dandum collecta.
but closed when giving.
